title: Identifying common errors
starter: Write down the last time a program of yours didn't work. Did it refuse to run, or run and do the wrong thing?
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Syntax errors
facts: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.
The program will not run at all: the translator reports the problem.
Typical causes: a missing bracket, a missing quotation mark, a misspelt keyword.
stations.challenge: Write three examples of syntax errors in a language you use.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.
Also credit: The program will not run at all: the translator reports the problem.

questions.q: What happens when a program contains a syntax error?
questions.a: It will not run: the translator reports the error

questions.q: Find the syntax error in this program.
questions.a: Line 4, a syntax error. Fix: Close the string: print('Running total: ', total)

stations.name: Logic errors
facts: A logic error follows the rules of the language but does the wrong thing.
The program runs to the end and produces an answer, which is wrong.
Typical causes: the wrong operator, the wrong order of tests, a loop that runs the wrong number of times.
stations.challenge: Describe a logic error that would not stop a program running.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A logic error follows the rules of the language but does the wrong thing.
Also credit: The program runs to the end and produces an answer, which is wrong.

questions.q: Find the logic error in this program, which should report a pass at 50 or more.
questions.a: Line 2, a logic error. Fix: Use >= so that a mark of exactly 50 passes

questions.q: Why are logic errors harder to find than syntax errors?
questions.a: The program runs without complaint, so nothing points to the mistake

stations.name: Telling them apart
facts: Ask one question: does the program run?
If it will not run, it is a syntax error.
If it runs but the answer is wrong, it is a logic error.
stations.challenge: Sort six mistakes into syntax and logic errors.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Ask one question: does the program run?
Also credit: If it will not run, it is a syntax error.

questions.q: Is each mistake a syntax error or a logic error?
questions.a: A missing closing bracket = Syntax error; Using + where - was meant = Logic error; Misspelling the keyword while = Syntax error; A loop that runs one time too many = Logic error; A missing quotation mark = Syntax error; Testing > instead of >= = Logic error

questions.q: A program outputs 11 when it should output 10. What kind of error is that?

stations.name: Finding the line
facts: For a syntax error, the translator usually names the line, or the one just after it.
For a logic error, work through the program by hand with a known input.
Compare what should happen at each line with what actually happens.
stations.challenge: Work through a short program by hand and find where it goes wrong.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: For a syntax error, the translator usually names the line, or the one just after it.
Also credit: For a logic error, work through the program by hand with a known input.

questions.q: This program should output the numbers 1 to 5. Find the error.
questions.a: Line 3, a syntax error. Fix: The loop variable must match: next i

questions.q: Why work through a program with a specific input?
questions.a: It shows exactly where what happens stops matching what should happen

stations.name: Suggesting a fix
facts: A fix should say what to change and what to change it to.
'Correct the error' earns nothing: 'change > to >=' earns the mark.
Check the fix does not break another case.
stations.challenge: Write a fix for a loop that runs one time too many.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A fix should say what to change and what to change it to.
Also credit: 'Correct the error' earns nothing: 'change > to >=' earns the mark.

questions.q: Which is the strongest suggested fix?
questions.a: On line 2, change > to >= so that a mark of exactly 50 passes

questions.q: This should add up the numbers 1 to 10 but outputs 0. Find the error.
questions.a: Line 5, a logic error. Fix: Print total, not total * 0

stations.name: Answering error questions
facts: State the line number, the type of error, and the fix.
Use the words syntax and logic: the marks are attached to them.
If the question gives line numbers, always quote them.
stations.challenge: Plan a four-mark answer identifying and fixing an error.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: State the line number, the type of error, and the fix.
Also credit: Use the words syntax and logic: the marks are attached to them.

questions.q: This program should print 'Well done' when the score is 10 or more. Find the error.
questions.a: Line 3, a logic error. Fix: Swap the outputs: 'Well done' belongs on the true branch

questions.q: A question is worth three marks for identifying and correcting an error. What are the three marks likely to be for?
questions.a: The line number, the type of error, and the correction

final.name: Final challenge: debug it

questions.q: This program should count down from 5 to 1. Find the error.
questions.a: Line 4, a logic error. Fix: Change n = n + 1 to n = n - 1

questions.q: Is each mistake a syntax error or a logic error?
questions.a: print('Hello) = Syntax error; Using * where + was meant = Logic error; Forgetting endif = Syntax error; A loop starting at 0 instead of 1 = Logic error; Writing whlie instead of while = Syntax error; Testing the lower grade boundary first = Logic error

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State the difference between a syntax error and a logic error.
points: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.
A logic error follows the rules of the language but does the wrong thing.
If it will not run, it is a syntax error.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: A program runs but always outputs one more than it should. What type of error is this? Explain your answer.
points: The program runs to the end and produces an answer, which is wrong.
If it runs but the answer is wrong, it is a logic error.
For a logic error, work through the program by hand with a known input.
A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

exam.q: Identify the error in the following program, state its type, and describe how to correct it.
points: State the line number, the type of error, and the fix.
For a logic error, work through the program by hand with a known input.
A syntax error breaks the rules of the language.
The program will not run at all: the translator reports the problem.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
